claim: Oscillatory behaviors are ubiquitous in transcriptional regulatory networks.
source: Oscillatory behaviors, which are ubiquitous in transcriptional regulatory networks, are often subject to inevitable biological noise.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract about the prevalence of oscillatory behaviors in transcriptional regulatory networks.

claim: Oscillatory behaviors in transcriptional regulatory networks are often subject to inevitable biological noise.
source: Oscillatory behaviors, which are ubiquitous in transcriptional regulatory networks, are often subject to inevitable biological noise.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact in the abstract.

claim: Topologies containing the repressilator with positive autoregulation show higher robustness of accurate oscillation than those containing the activator-inhibitor oscillator when facing parameter variability (extrinsic noise).
source: We find that, no matter what source of the noise is applied, the topologies containing the repressilator with positive autoregulation show higher robustness of accurate oscillation than those containing the activator-inhibitor oscillator, and additional positive autoregulation enhances the robustness against noise.
evidence: This finding is based on systematic exploration of network topologies and their robustness to noise as described in the Results section.

claim: Additional positive autoregulation enhances the robustness against noise.
source: We find that, no matter what source of the noise is applied, the topologies containing the repressilator with positive autoregulation show higher robustness of accurate oscillation than those containing the activator-inhibitor oscillator, and additional positive autoregulation enhances the robustness against noise.
evidence: This is a key finding from the systematic analysis of network topologies.

claim: Parameter variability is buffered by long period.
source: Nevertheless, the attenuation of different sources of noise is governed by distinct mechanisms: the parameter variability is buffered by the long period, while the stochasticity of chemical reactions is filtered by the high amplitude.
evidence: This mechanism is identified through analysis of the relationship between period/amplitude and robustness to different noise sources.

claim: The stochasticity of chemical reactions is filtered by high amplitude.
source: Nevertheless, the attenuation of different sources of noise is governed by distinct mechanisms: the parameter variability is buffered by the long period, while the stochasticity of chemical reactions is filtered by the high amplitude.
evidence: This mechanism is identified through analysis of the relationship between period/amplitude and robustness to different noise sources.

claim: Adding a repressilator to the activator-inhibitor oscillator improves oscillation accuracy compared to the topology with only an activator-inhibitor oscillator in a synthetic human NF-κB signaling network.
source: Furthermore, we analyze the noise of a synthetic human nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling network by varying three different topologies and verify that the addition of a repressilator to the activator-inhibitor oscillator, which leads to the emergence of high-robustness motif—the repressilator with positive autoregulation—improves the oscillation accuracy in comparison to the topology with only an activator-inhibitor oscillator.
evidence: This is experimentally validated using synthetic NF-κB circuits as described in the Results section.

claim: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in cell cycle.
source: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in a broad range of biological processes, such as cell cycle (Ferrell et al., 2011; Tyson, 1991), circadian rhythms (Partch et al., 2014), and mitotic wave in Drosophila embryo (Deneke et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in circadian rhythms.
source: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in a broad range of biological processes, such as cell cycle (Ferrell et al., 2011; Tyson, 1991), circadian rhythms (Partch et al., 2014), and mitotic wave in Drosophila embryo (Deneke et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in mitotic wave in Drosophila embryo.
source: Oscillatory behaviors have been observed in a broad range of biological processes, such as cell cycle (Ferrell et al., 2011; Tyson, 1991), circadian rhythms (Partch et al., 2014), and mitotic wave in Drosophila embryo (Deneke et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Oscillatory features including period and amplitude can encode functional information.
source: Oscillatory features, including period and amplitude, can encode functional information, which plays an essential role in coordinating gene regulation (Cai et al., 2008) or transmitting distinct stimuli (Hao and O'Shea, 2012; Heltberg et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Negative feedback, time delay, and nonlinearity have been identified as key mechanisms for biochemical oscillation.
source: In past decades, negative feedback, time delay, and nonlinearity have been identified as key mechanisms for biochemical oscillation (Novák and Tyson, 2008), following which researchers artificially synthesized biochemical networks capable of oscillation (Atkinson et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2015; Elowitz and Leibler, 2000; Potvin-Trottier et al., 2016; Stricker et al., 2008; Tigges et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Researchers have artificially synthesized biochemical networks capable of oscillation.
source: In past decades, negative feedback, time delay, and nonlinearity have been identified as key mechanisms for biochemical oscillation (Novák and Tyson, 2008), following which researchers artificially synthesized biochemical networks capable of oscillation (Atkinson et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2015; Elowitz and Leibler, 2000; Potvin-Trottier et al., 2016; Stricker et al., 2008; Tigges et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Repressilator and activator-inhibitor oscillator are the most famous synthetic oscillators.
source: Repressilator (Elowitz and Leibler, 2000) and activator-inhibitor oscillator (Atkinson et al., 2003) are the most famous of these synthetic oscillators.
evidence: This is stated as a known fact with citations.

claim: Many synthetic biological circuits that can oscillate have typically irregular dynamics owing to ubiquitous biological noise.
source: While many synthetic biological circuits can oscillate, their dynamics are typically irregular, owing to ubiquitous biological noise such as fluctuations in the microenvironment and inherent stochasticity of chemical reactions (Elowitz et al., 2002; Li et al., 2009; Potvin-Trottier et al., 2016; Raser and O'Shea, 2004; Swain et al., 2002; Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Biological noise includes fluctuations in the microenvironment and inherent stochasticity of chemical reactions.
source: While many synthetic biological circuits can oscillate, their dynamics are typically irregular, owing to ubiquitous biological noise such as fluctuations in the microenvironment and inherent stochasticity of chemical reactions (Elowitz et al., 2002; Li et al., 2009; Potvin-Trottier et al., 2016; Raser and O'Shea, 2004; Swain et al., 2002; Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Many kinetic parameters can influence the robustness of biological oscillators, such as system size and degree of cooperativity of reactions.
source: Previous studies revealed that many kinetic parameters can influence the robustness of the biological oscillators, such as the system size and degree of cooperativity of reactions (Gonze et al., 2002a), timescale of the promoter interaction (Forger and Peskin, 2005), repressor degradation rate (Potvin-Trottier et al., 2016), free energy cost measured by ATP/ADP ratios (Cao et al., 2015; Fei et al., 2018; Qin et al., 2021), and kinetic parameter-determined oscillation mechanisms (i.e., limit cycle or force driving) (Monti et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: There exists a relationship between network configurations and noise buffering capabilities for biochemical oscillators.
source: Moreover, growing evidence suggests the existence of the relationship between network configurations and noise buffering capabilities for biochemical oscillators.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from previous studies.

claim: Adding negative autoregulation to the negative feedback loop in a synthetic microbial consortium oscillator increases the parameter space to oscillate persistently in the face of noise.
source: For example, in a synthetic microbial consortium oscillator composed of two different types of bacteria, adding negative autoregulation to the negative feedback loop increases the parameter space to oscillate persistently in the face of noise (Chen et al., 2015); an additional positive feedback loop in the biochemical oscillator consisting of the negative feedback loop can decrease the coefficient of variation (CV) of period when considering the stochasticity of reactions (Mather et al., 2009) and possess nearly constant period when varying the synthesis rate (Stricker et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: An additional positive feedback loop in the biochemical oscillator consisting of the negative feedback loop can decrease the coefficient of variation (CV) of period when considering the stochasticity of reactions.
source: For example, in a synthetic microbial consortium oscillator composed of two different types of bacteria, adding negative autoregulation to the negative feedback loop increases the parameter space to oscillate persistently in the face of noise (Chen et al., 2015); an additional positive feedback loop in the biochemical oscillator consisting of the negative feedback loop can decrease the coefficient of variation (CV) of period when considering the stochasticity of reactions (Mather et al., 2009) and possess nearly constant period when varying the synthesis rate (Stricker et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: An additional positive feedback loop in the biochemical oscillator consisting of the negative feedback loop can possess nearly constant period when varying the synthesis rate.
source: For example, in a synthetic microbial consortium oscillator composed of two different types of bacteria, adding negative autoregulation to the negative feedback loop increases the parameter space to oscillate persistently in the face of noise (Chen et al., 2015); an additional positive feedback loop in the biochemical oscillator consisting of the negative feedback loop can decrease the coefficient of variation (CV) of period when considering the stochasticity of reactions (Mather et al., 2009) and possess nearly constant period when varying the synthesis rate (Stricker et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: The study systematically explores the relationship between network topology and robustness to different sources of noise in both two- and three-node networks.
source: Here, we systematically explore the relationship between the network topology and robustness to different sources of noise in both two- and three-node networks.
evidence: This describes the approach taken in the study.

claim: The study performs an exhausting search of two- and three-node network topologies to identify those capable of oscillation in the absence of noise.
source: We first perform an exhausting search of two- and three-node network topologies to identify those capable of oscillation in the absence of noise, and then investigate the abilities of those oscillatory topologies to achieve accurate oscillation in the presence of different sources of noise.
evidence: This describes the methodology of the study.

claim: Two different sources of noise are considered: extrinsic noise (parameters perturbed by noise terms whose magnitudes are proportional to parameters) and intrinsic noise (stochasticity due to small copy number of proteins from chemical reactions).
source: Two different sources are considered: parameters are perturbed by noise terms whose magnitudes are proportional to parameters (i.e., extrinsic noise); chemical reactions induce stochasticity due to a small copy number of proteins (i.e., intrinsic noise).
evidence: This describes the types of noise modeled in the study.

claim: All oscillatory topologies are classified according to what core motifs they include.
source: We classify all oscillatory topologies according to what core motifs they include, and then compare the ability to execute accurate oscillation in the presence of noise among different categories.
evidence: This describes the analysis approach.

claim: Two categories whose core motifs include a repressilator with a positive feedback perform better than others.
source: Two categories whose core motifs include a repressilator with a positive feedback perform better than others.
evidence: This is a key finding from the analysis.

claim: The existence of positive autoregulation always enhances the performance of oscillatory networks against noise.
source: Importantly, the existence of positive autoregulation always enhances the performance.
evidence: This is a key finding from the analysis.

claim: Long period buffers extrinsic noise.
source: While these results hold regardless of what source of noise exists, mechanisms to attenuate different sources of noise are distinct: long period buffers the extrinsic noise, and high amplitude attenuates the intrinsic noise.
evidence: This mechanism is identified through analysis.

claim: High amplitude attenuates intrinsic noise.
source: While these results hold regardless of what source of noise exists, mechanisms to attenuate different sources of noise are distinct: long period buffers the extrinsic noise, and high amplitude attenuates the intrinsic noise.
evidence: This mechanism is identified through analysis.

claim: Adding a repressilator to the activator-inhibitor topology in synthetic NF-κB signaling circuits can improve the performance to buffer noise.
source: Moreover, we experimentally validate that adding a repressilator to the activator-inhibitor topology in synthetic NF-κB signaling circuits can improve the performance to buffer noise, indicating the important role of the repressilator with a positive autoregulation in filtering noise.
evidence: This is experimentally validated.

claim: The repressilator with positive autoregulation plays an important role in filtering noise.
source: Moreover, we experimentally validate that adding a repressilator to the activator-inhibitor topology in synthetic NF-κB signaling circuits can improve the performance to buffer noise, indicating the important role of the repressilator with a positive autoregulation in filtering noise.
evidence: This is inferred from experimental validation.

claim: The dimensionless correlation time (τ/T) is used to measure the accuracy of oscillatory behavior.
source: To measure the accuracy of the oscillatory behavior, we use the dimensionless correlation time, which is the correlation time τ divided by the period T.
evidence: This describes the metric used in the study.

claim: The correlation time τ describes how fast the autocorrelation function C(t) exponentially decays.
source: The correlation time τ describes how fast the autocorrelation function C(t) exponentially decays.
evidence: This defines the correlation time metric.

claim: For a noisy dynamic trajectory of the oscillator, the autocorrelation function C(t) displays a damped oscillation.
source: To be specific, for a noisy dynamic trajectory of the oscillator, C(t) displays a damped oscillation (Figure 1A)
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: If fluctuations of the noisy trajectory are small, the autocorrelation decays slowly, leading to a large value of τ.
source: If fluctuations of the noisy trajectory are small, the autocorrelation decays slowly, leading to a large value of τ.
evidence: This explains the relationship between trajectory fluctuations and correlation time.

claim: The number of all two- and three-node network topologies is 39.
source: Besides, the number of all two- and three-node network topologies is 39 because there are nine links in total and each link has three options: activation, inhibition, or does not exist; however, by excluding topologies with isolated nodes or symmetrical to existing topologies, the number of possible two- and three-node network topologies is reduced from 39 to 1955.
evidence: This is calculated based on the combinatorial possibilities.

claim: By excluding topologies with isolated nodes or symmetrical to existing topologies, the number of possible two- and three-node network topologies is reduced from 39 to 1955.
source: Besides, the number of all two- and three-node network topologies is 39 because there are nine links in total and each link has three options: activation, inhibition, or does not exist; however, by excluding topologies with isolated nodes or symmetrical to existing topologies, the number of possible two- and three-node network topologies is reduced from 39 to 1955.
evidence: This is calculated based on the combinatorial possibilities after applying constraints.

claim: For the activator-inhibitor topology, the activator (node A) has a positive autoregulation and positively regulates the inhibitor (node B), but is negatively regulated by the inhibitor.
source: For the activator-inhibitor topology, the activator (node A) has a positive autoregulation and positively regulates the inhibitor (node B), but is negatively regulated by the inhibitor
evidence: This describes the structure of the activator-inhibitor topology.

claim: For the repressilator topology, each node acts as a repressor to inhibit its next node, thus constituting a cyclic negative-feedback loop.
source: for the repressilator topology, each node acts as a repressor to inhibit its next node, thus constituting a cyclic negative-feedback loop.
evidence: This describes the structure of the repressilator topology.

claim: Transcriptional regulations are used to describe interactions among nodes in the mathematical model.
source: To model two- and three-node network topologies, we use transcriptional regulations to describe interactions among nodes (Figure 1D; see 'Methods').
evidence: This describes the modeling approach.

claim: In a transcriptional regulatory network, nodes and links represent genes' products and transcriptional regulations, respectively.
source: In a transcriptional regulatory network, nodes and links represent genes' products and transcriptional regulations, respectively
evidence: This defines the components of the model.

claim: When multiple transcription factors regulate the same gene simultaneously, the competitive inhibition logic is adopted.
source: Moreover, when multiple transcription factors regulate the same gene simultaneously, the competitive inhibition logic is adopted: those transcription factors compete for the same binding sites.
evidence: This describes the modeling assumption.

claim: Extrinsic noise is modeled as the variability of parameters including the maximum production rate v and the degradation rate r.
source: On the one hand, we model the extrinsic noise as the variability of parameters including the maximum production rate v and the degradation rate r (Figure 1E; see 'Methods'): each of these parameters is added by a noise term with zero mean, and the standard deviation of the noise term is proportional to the value of the kinetic parameter.
evidence: This describes how extrinsic noise is modeled.

claim: Intrinsic noise is modeled by directly simulating the dynamics of molecular numbers rather than concentrations.
source: On the other hand, the intrinsic noise, generated by the stochasticity of discrete chemical reactions, is modeled by directly simulating the dynamics of molecular numbers rather than concentrations.
evidence: This describes how intrinsic noise is modeled.

claim: The Gillespie algorithm can exactly solve the stochastic process of intrinsic noise.
source: This stochastic process can be exactly solved by the Gillespie algorithm, which has been widely used in previous studies (Liu et al., 2020; Thattai and van Oudenaarden, 2001; Veliz-Cuba et al., 2015; Zhao et al., 2021)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Chemical Langevin equations are used as approximations to reduce the computation cost of the Gillespie algorithm.
source: however, the computation cost is high, and thus we use chemical Langevin equations as approximations to reduce the cost (Gillespie, 2000).
evidence: This describes the computational approach used.

claim: 474 oscillatory network topologies were obtained from the search.
source: In this way, we finally obtain 474 oscillatory network topologies, and nearly 35% of them are with the repressilator.
evidence: This is the result of the systematic search.

claim: Nearly 35% of the 474 oscillatory network topologies contain the repressilator.
source: In this way, we finally obtain 474 oscillatory network topologies, and nearly 35% of them are with the repressilator.
evidence: This is the result of the systematic search.

claim: Five types of core motifs are used to classify all 474 oscillatory network topologies.
source: We start by classifying all 474 oscillatory network topologies according to five types of core motifs.
evidence: This describes the classification approach.

claim: The first core motif is composed of the repressilator and a positive autoregulation, but the node with the positive autoregulation is not allowed to have a positive incoming link.
source: These five types of core motifs are as follows: the first core motif (shown in brown in Figure 2A) is composed of the repressilator and a positive autoregulation, but the node with the positive autoregulation is not allowed to have a positive incoming link
evidence: This defines the first core motif category.

claim: The second core motif is similar to the first core motif except that the positive incoming link to the positive autoregulated node is required.
source: the second core motif (shown in orange in Figure 2A) is similar to the first core motif except that the positive incoming link to the positive autoregulated node is required
evidence: This defines the second core motif category.

claim: The third type of core motifs include the activator-inhibitor topology and its two variants.
source: the third type of core motifs include the activator-inhibitor topology and its two variants (shown in green in Figure 2A)
evidence: This defines the third core motif category.

claim: The fourth and fifth core motifs are the repressilator and delayed negative feedback.
source: the fourth and fifth core motifs are the repressilator and delayed negative feedback (Figure 2A), respectively.
evidence: This defines the fourth and fifth core motif categories.

claim: All oscillatory network topologies have a negative feedback structure.
source: Note that these oscillatory network topologies all have a negative feedback structure, which is consistent with previous studies (Glass and Pasternack, 1978; Novák and Tyson, 2008).
evidence: This observation is consistent with previous studies.

claim: The order of C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5 categories according to the robustness of accurate oscillation to extrinsic noise is C1 > C2 > C3 > C4 > C5.
source: These findings indicate that the order of these five categories according to the robustness of accurate oscillation to extrinsic noise is C1 > C2 > C3 > C4 > C5.

claim: Topologies containing the repressilator with positive autoregulation achieve higher robustness against extrinsic noise than those containing the activator-inhibitor topology.
source: The facts that C1 > C3 and C2 > C3 demonstrate that topologies containing the repressilator with positive autoregulation achieve higher robustness against extrinsic noise than those containing the activator-inhibitor topology.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of category robustness.

claim: The higher robustness of C1 and C2 categories than C4 category against extrinsic noise is due to the effect of positive autoregulation in improving the robustness to extrinsic noise.
source: Besides, core motifs in both C1 and C2 categories have an extra positive autoregulation in comparison to the core motif (the repressilator) in C4 category, suggesting that the higher robustness of C1 and C2 categories than C4 category against extrinsic noise is due to the effect of positive autoregulation in improving the robustness to extrinsic noise.

claim: The comparison of the robustness between C3 and C5 categories validates the effect of positive autoregulation on improving robustness to extrinsic noise.
source: This effect is also validated by the comparison of the robustness between C3 and C5 categories.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of category robustness.

claim: The category with combined core motifs usually shows intermediate robustness among its 'component' categories.
source: It can be seen that the category with combined core motifs usually shows intermediate robustness among its 'component' categories.
evidence: This is observed from the data in Figure 2C.

claim: If a network topology has low robustness against extrinsic noise, adding a high-robustness core motif usually improves the robustness, but the combined topology cannot outperform the added high-robustness core motif.
source: That is to say, if a network topology has low robustness against extrinsic noise, adding a high-robustness core motif usually improves the robustness, but the combined topology cannot outperform the added high-robustness core motif.
evidence: This is inferred from the data on combined topologies.

claim: The Spearman coefficient between Topt and 90 percentile of τ/T for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.94.
source: The Spearman coefficient between Topt and 90 percentile of τ/T for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.94, which is larger than that between Aopt and 90 percentile of τ/T (0.88).

claim: The robustness to extrinsic noise is more highly correlated with long period rather than high amplitude.

claim: The ranking of C1, C2, C3, C4, and C5 categories according to Topt is C1 > C2 ≈ C3 > C4 > C5.
source: The ranking of these five categories according to Topt is C1 > C2 ≈ C3 > C4 > C5, which is obtained by the one-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum tests for each adjacent two categories.

claim: The topology with long period usually leads to high robustness of accurate oscillation to extrinsic noise.
source: This ranking is almost the same as that according to the robustness of accurate oscillation to extrinsic noise (C1 > C2 > C3 > C4 > C5) except rankings for C2 and C3 categories, suggesting that the topology with long period usually leads to high robustness of accurate oscillation to extrinsic noise (Figure 2G).

claim: C2 category might show better robustness to extrinsic noise than C3 category though they have the same period.
source: The only inconsistency is that C2 and C3 categories differ in the robustness but have no significant difference in the probability to achieve long period. That is to say, C2 category might show better robustness to extrinsic noise than C3 category though they have the same period.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of robustness and period.

claim: Topologies with prolonged period tend to have good performance to filter extrinsic noise.
source: These findings suggest that topologies with prolonged period tend to have good performance to filter extrinsic noise, and this correlation is less likely due to that they have different amplitude.
evidence: This is inferred from the analysis of dynamics with similar amplitude but different periods.

claim: 90 percentiles of the dimensionless correlation time (τ/T) in the presence of only intrinsic noise show a roughly similar trend from C1 to C5 categories as in the presence of extrinsic noise.
source: With the same oscillatory network topology categories present in Figure 2A, 90 percentiles of the dimensionless correlation time (τ/T) in the presence of only intrinsic noise also show a roughly similar trend from C1 to C5 categories (Figure 3A) except that C2 category exhibits the same robustness with C1 category to intrinsic noise while C2 category shows lower robustness than C1 in the presence of extrinsic noise.

claim: C2 category exhibits the same robustness with C1 category to intrinsic noise while C2 category shows lower robustness than C1 in the presence of extrinsic noise.
source: With the same oscillatory network topology categories present in Figure 2A, 90 percentiles of the dimensionless correlation time (τ/T) in the presence of only intrinsic noise also show a roughly similar trend from C1 to C5 categories (Figure 3A) except that C2 category exhibits the same robustness with C1 category to intrinsic noise while C2 category shows lower robustness than C1 in the presence of extrinsic noise.
evidence: This is observed from the data.

source: Moreover, the higher robustness of C1 and C2 categories compared with C3 category validates the better performance of the repressilator with positive autoregulation than the activator-inhibitor topology
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of category robustness.

source: the improvement of robustness from C4 category to C1 (or C2) category indicates the effect of positive autoregulation on the robustness to intrinsic noise

claim: The comparison between the robustness of C5 and C3 categories implies the advantage of the positive autoregulation against intrinsic noise.
source: the comparison between the robustness of C5 and C3 categories also implies the advantage of the positive autoregulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of category robustness.

claim: The hybrid of core motifs imparts an intermediate robustness in the presence of intrinsic noise.
source: Another consistency is that the hybrid of core motifs imparts an intermediate robustness not only in the presence of the extrinsic noise (Figure 2C) but also in the presence of the intrinsic noise (Figure 3B).

claim: In the presence of only intrinsic noise, the Spearman correlation coefficient of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Topt for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.72.
source: In the presence of only intrinsic noise, the Spearman correlation coefficient of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Topt for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.72, which is smaller than that of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Aopt (0.81) (Figure 3C).

claim: In the presence of only intrinsic noise, the Spearman correlation coefficient of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Aopt for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.81.
source: In the presence of only intrinsic noise, the Spearman correlation coefficient of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Topt for all 474 oscillatory network topologies is 0.72, which is smaller than that of 90 percentiles of τ/T and Aopt (0.81) (Figure 3C).

claim: The robustness of accurate oscillation against intrinsic noise is more highly correlated with amplitude than period.
source: These findings suggest that unlike the case of extrinsic noise where the robustness is more strongly correlated with period, the robustness of accurate oscillation against intrinsic noise is more highly correlated with amplitude.
evidence: This is inferred from the Spearman correlation coefficients.

claim: The topology with the high amplitude has a larger probability to achieve high robustness against intrinsic noise than that with long period.
source: In other words, the topology with the high amplitude has a larger probability to achieve high robustness against intrinsic noise than that with long period.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation analysis.

claim: The relation between the amplitude and robustness to intrinsic noise is not very strong.
source: However, it should be noted that the correlation coefficient between 90 percentiles of τ/T and Aopt for all oscillatory network topologies is not very close to 1 (the right panel in Figure 3C), and it is also much smaller than 1 even in each category (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), implying that the relation between the amplitude and robustness to intrinsic noise is not very strong, and that some topologies with small amplitude may perform better than those with high amplitude.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation coefficients.

claim: There might exist other mechanisms to attenuate intrinsic noise besides high amplitude.
source: However, it should be noted that the correlation coefficient between 90 percentiles of τ/T and Aopt for all oscillatory network topologies is not very close to 1 (the right panel in Figure 3C), and it is also much smaller than 1 even in each category (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), implying that the relation between the amplitude and robustness to intrinsic noise is not very strong, and that some topologies with small amplitude may perform better than those with high amplitude. Therefore, there might exist other mechanisms to attenuate intrinsic noise.
evidence: This is inferred from the imperfect correlation.

claim: The ranking of five network topology categories according to amplitude is C1 > C2≈ C3 > C4 > C5.
source: Furthermore, by applying Wilcoxon rank-sum tests to amplitude average (Aopt) for neighboring two categories, we find that the ranking of five network topology categories according to amplitude is C1 > C2≈ C3 > C4 > C5 (Figure 3D).

claim: The ranking of five network topology categories according to robustness to intrinsic noise is C1 ≈ C2 > C3 > C4 > C5.

claim: The amplitude might link the topology category and the robustness to intrinsic noise.

claim: The high amplitude is not the only mechanism to enhance the robustness to intrinsic noise.
source: The only exception is C2 category: because of the fact that C1 > C2 ≈ C3 according to Aopt and the fact that the amplitude strongly correlates with the robustness, the C2 category is supposed to show the same robustness to intrinsic noise as C3 category and exhibit lower robustness than C1 category; however, the robustness to intrinsic noise for C2 category is actually at the same level of C1 category, further demonstrating that the high amplitude is not the only mechanism to enhance the robustness to intrinsic noise (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the exception in the ranking pattern.

claim: Simulations using the Gillespie algorithm lead to similar conclusions as chemical Langevin equations regarding the repressilator with positive autoregulation performing better than the activator-inhibitor.
source: According to the robustness rankings for C1–C5 categories, the repressilator with positive autoregulation performs better than the activator-inhibitor, and the topologies with positive autoregulation are better than that without positive autoregulation.
evidence: This is observed from simulations using the Gillespie algorithm.

claim: The robustness is more correlated with the mean amplitude rather than the mean period when using the Gillespie algorithm.
source: Besides, the robustness is more correlated with the mean amplitude rather than the mean period, and the order of the five categories sorted by the mean amplitude is almost the same as that sorted by robustness, indicating the bridge role of amplitude to link topologies and the robustness to intrinsic noise.
evidence: This is observed from simulations using the Gillespie algorithm.

claim: The Gillespie algorithm leads to higher dimensionless correlation times than chemical Langevin equations.
source: We also find that the Gillespie algorithm leads to higher dimensionless correlation times than chemical Langevin equations since the maximal correlation in Figure 3A is near 6 and that in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A is 40.
